Every Wendrel number has a Talley weight.why: Everything is made up: a class of numbers and a property given to it. Both names have at most one Dolma hit and no mathematical use on the web.

sources.note: No number of that name; hits were Wendt's determinant and Welschinger numbers.
No 'Talley weight' in mathematics (nearest: a 'tally' statistic on Young tableaux). The class name first tried here, 'sorrel number', was dropped because a 2026 Gauss contest uses 'Sorrol number'.

4 is a perfect square..why: 4 = 2 × 2, the first square after 1; stated very often.
